story.what_it_does: Rainbow Children's Medicare runs a hospital chain in India focused on children's and women's care. FY2025-26 revenue was about ₹17,031 million, up 12%, and it is adding hospitals in South India, North India and Mumbai.
story.plans: Management plans to add about 2,500 beds over five years at an estimated capex of ₹2,200 crore, funded from internal resources. Openings include Indore (Q3 FY27), Malad Mumbai (Q1 FY28), and Coimbatore and Gurugram hospitals (Q3 FY28 onward). It also targets revenue above ₹2,000 crore this year and growth of about 20%.
story.moat: The notes show mature hospitals earning higher revenue per occupied bed (about ₹70,000 vs ₹59,000 for hospitals under five years old) and a strong cash position of about ₹613 crore with no debt. Management itself rates its sales and marketing at only 30 to 40 versus leading peers and says Hyderabad competition is rising, so the notes show no clearly proven durable edge.

scenarios.story: New hospitals ramp up and occupancy rises toward the 55-60% targets, helping revenue grow around 20% and margins recover toward management's aspiration. Internal cash funds the expansion without debt.
signals_to_watch: Blended occupancy moving toward the 56% target from 41.2% in Q1 FY27
Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 23.2% being sustained at about 20%

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing at double digits, helped partly by acquisitions, while new hospitals dilute margins as they ramp up. Profit grows more slowly than revenue (PAT up 10.9% in Q2 FY27 vs revenue up 23.2%).
signals_to_watch: EBITDA margin trend (28.6% in Q1 FY27, 31.0% in Q2 FY27)
Mature hospital occupancy (54.2% in Q2 FY27 vs 54.5% a year earlier)

scenarios.story: Occupancy stays low as many new beds open, and new hospitals keep losing money. Competition, seasonality and weak international patient flows could keep pressure on profit.
signals_to_watch: New hospitals cluster EBITDA of -16% in Q2 FY27 (pre Ind AS 116)
Further timeline delays, like Coimbatore moving to H2 FY28 and then Q3 FY28
